question: Should provider-managed contextual embeddings extend the generic memory embedding API, become a separate memory-backend capability, or remain an external integration?
rationale: The existing seam handles flat embeddings and asymmetric labels, but grouped-document requests, persistent index identity, result metadata, and rollback ownership require a durable product and compatibility decision.

options.title: Extend Generic Plugin API
options.body: Add provider-neutral contextual document/query operations and index-fingerprint semantics, then implement Voyage through its provider plugin.

options.title: Use Separate Memory Backend
options.body: Keep flat embedding providers unchanged and require contextual systems to own indexing, storage, diagnostics, and rollback as a memory plugin.

options.title: Keep External For Now
options.body: Leave native memory unchanged and document contextual embedding systems as third-party memory integrations until demand or API design matures.

recommendation.title: Extend Generic Plugin API
recommendation.body: Add provider-neutral contextual document/query operations and index-fingerprint semantics, then implement Voyage through its provider plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this handle to recent memory-plugin scope and release decisions.
